text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- There are fears that four locomotives supplied to Nigerian railways by China under a contract to revamp the rail sector may be refurbished ones and not new one as contracted.
- A new president is soon to be elected for the Nigerian Stock Exchange following the expiration of the tenure of banker Pascal Dozie, capital market sources say.
- The owners of beer maker Bendel Brewery in the midwest are seeking to list its shares on the Nigerian stock exchange.
- The federal government is set to release 50 billion naira to ministries and government agencies, being their first quarter budget allocation. The money was held up so as not stoke inflation.

- A judicial commission of inquiry into recent communal clashes in the oil-producing Delta state over relocation of a local council headquarters is to be instituted next week, says the state military administrator Colonel John Dungs.

- National carrier Nigeria Airways will resume international flights on Friday, starting with the lucrative Lagos-London route, following the resolution of a disagreement over payment of premiums to state insurer NICON.
- Commercial Bank Credit Lyonnais declares 333.076 million naira profit for 1996 versus 252.967 million naira in 1995.
- Elf Nigeria last month began the construction of its $400 million Obite gas project, a major boost for the $4 billion Nigeria liquefied natural gas project.
- No fewer than 16 African first ladies have arrived in the capital Abuja for their three-day summit opening there on Monday on promoting peace in Africa.
- Federal government may consult political parties this week over the election timetable in its transition to civil rule programme.
